title: A Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning Engine for Compilation-Free Patch Presence Testing
abstract: arXiv:2610.27871v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Code reuse in modern software ecosystems facilitates the spread of 1-day vulnerabilities, posing significant security risks. Determining if patches are present is crucial, but traditional methods suffer from limited usability and accuracy, often depending on a fragile compilation process. In our prior work, we introduced Lares, the first compilation-free framework for patch presence testing that combines large language models (LLMs) with SMT solvers. However, Lares treats the LLM and the SMT solver as two separate, parallel decision channels: the symbolic channel (Z3) succeeded in only 20% of code cases, and the remaining cases fell back to the neural channel (the LLM) for the final decision. Letting the LLM act as the final arbiter turns verification into an informal, non-deterministic process that is prone to hallucination errors, while the two channels never reinforce each other. translated_title: 用于免编译补丁存在性检测的神经符号推理引擎
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.27871v1 Announce Type: new 摘要：现代软件生态系统中的代码复用促进了1-day漏洞的传播，带来了重大的安全风险。判断补丁是否存在至关重要，但传统方法存在可用性和准确性有限的问题，且往往依赖于脆弱的编译过程。在我们之前的工作中，我们提出了Lares，这是首个将大语言模型（LLM）与SMT求解器相结合的免编译补丁存在性检测框架。然而，Lares将LLM和SMT求解器视为两个相互独立、并行的决策通道：符号通道（Z3）仅在20%的代码用例中成功，其余用例则回退到神经通道（LLM）进行最终决策。让LLM充当最终仲裁者，使验证变成了一个非正式、非确定性的过程，容易产生幻觉错误，同时两个通道之间也从未相互增强。为了克服这些局限，我们提出了SyLares，……
tldr: 该论文提出SyLares，一种深度融合大语言模型与SMT求解器的神经符号推理引擎，克服了此前Lares框架中两通道并行、LLM充当最终仲裁者导致的幻觉问题，实现了更可靠的免编译补丁存在性检测。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes SyLares, a neuro-symbolic reasoning engine that deeply integrates LLMs with SMT solvers rather than treating them as parallel decision channels, overcoming the hallucination-prone fallback design of its predecessor Lares to enable more reliable compilation-free patch presence testing.
